title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
head: 9007cee1

claims.claim: The analyzer no longer throws on duplicate int keys, duplicate string keys or mixed key kinds; it reports MsgPack005 instead, with or without SuppressSourceGeneration.
claims.why_this_tier: 4 new tests fail on base (MsgPack005 plus AD0001 from an analyzer exception) and pass on the branch.

claims.claim: For every list of 1 to 4 keyed members with int or string keys, the real TypeCollector does not throw on the branch; on base it threw on most of them.
claims.why_this_tier: Chain: the Dafny model proves it for all lists, and the model matches the real C# on every input up to 4 members; the C# run throws on base and not on the branch, so the weakest link is Tested.

chain.link: model matches real TypeCollector on 3710 inputs (base and branch, 0 mismatches)

claims.claim: The fix is incomplete: when a type's first keyed member is a field with [Key(null)], the analyzer still throws (AD0001, ArgumentNullException), also with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
claims.why_this_tier: A probe on the real analyzer reproduces the crash on base and on the branch, so no test fails on base and passes on the branch; the tier rules give a reproduced gap no machine tier.

claims.claim: The new `continue` also skips collecting the member's type, so a member with a mixed key and an unserializable type no longer gets MsgPack003 (base reported it when the first key was a string).
claims.why_this_tier: It drops a warning that base reported; whether that is acceptable next to the MsgPack005 error on the same member is a product call.

claims.claim: When two members share a key, the first member is kept and the second gets MsgPack005 ('must be unique'); no repeated key goes unreported.
claims.why_this_tier: The duplicate-key tests fail on base and pass on the branch, and the model lemma DupReported matches the real C# on every input up to 4 members.

chain.link: Dafny lemma DupReported (first wins, every repeat reported)
model matches real TypeCollector on 3710 inputs
duplicate-key tests fail on base, pass on branch

claims.claim: The same fix is pasted into both the properties loop and the fields loop, which adds duplicated code to TypeCollector.cs.
claims.why_this_tier: The numbers come from a clone and complexity script run on base and branch.

claims.claim: 4 of the 8 new analyzer tests (missing key, AllowPrivate, member type, generation-only diagnostics) already pass on base; they pin existing behaviour and are not evidence for the fix.
claims.why_this_tier: The count comes from the old-versus-new test runner.

claims.claim: A suppressed type gets no generated formatter and still round-trips through the dynamic resolver (the 2 new execution tests).
claims.why_this_tier: The execution test project does not build in our environment on base or branch, because the source generator is not loaded (CS9057), so the tests never ran.

claims.claim: The new README section says the analyzer validates suppressed types (MsgPack003, 004, 005, 012, 015) and skips MsgPack011, 016 and 017 for them.
claims.why_this_tier: It is documentation. Tests cover 003, 004, 005, 015 and the skipped ones, but not 012, and C-2234-03 shows a case where MsgPack005 validation still crashes.

found: We found (probe, real analyzer): the new `continue` skips CollectCore for the member's type, so MsgPack003 is lost for a mixed-key member (C-2234-04).

We found (probe, real analyzer, Dafny model): a first field with [Key(null)] still crashes the analyzer with ArgumentNullException, on base and branch, with SuppressSourceGeneration too. The properties loop guards with `else if (stringKey is not null)`; the fields loop uses a bare `else` (C-2234-03).

The theorem in the brief ('collecting keys never fails, whatever keys repeat or mix kinds') is false for the real code. Dafny proves the exact condition instead: it fails if and only if the first keyed member is a field with [Key(null)].
Finding (b) dropped: the second member of a repeated key gets MsgPack005 on the branch, and the first one is kept (C-2234-05).

The base crash on repeated keys also happens without SuppressSourceGeneration (test DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes fails on base). The bug is not specific to suppressed types, and 4 of the 8 analyzer tests show the analyzer already validated suppressed types on base.
SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.cs raises StyleCop SA1649 (file name does not match first type name).
Pre-existing, outside the diff: the fields-loop BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic passes no message arguments, so the message reads 'Both int and string keys are null: {0}.{1}'.

refused.what: C-2234-04: the `continue` drops MsgPack003 for mixed-key members
refused.why: Dropping a diagnostic that base reported is a product call for the analyzer owner.

scope_drift: README.md gains a 14-line 'Opting out of source generation' section. The issue title asks for an analyzer fix, not documentation.
not_checked: The 2 execution tests (SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.cs): the project does not build here because the generator needs compiler 4.12 and SDK 8.0.402 has 4.11 (CS9057).
Source generator output (reportDiagnostic is null in the generator path) for repeated or mixed keys: what code is emitted when the first member wins.
MsgPack012 (inaccessible types) for suppressed types, which the README claims.
The full test suite on the branch; only the new tests and our probes were run.
Members without any [Key] attribute, inherited members, records with positional parameters: not in the model's input domain.
The model's input domain is keys 0, 1, "a", "b" and null, with up to 4 members, so the model-vs-C# check covers 3710 inputs, not all inputs.
The issue body: only the issue title was available to us.
